description: BAT48 small-signal Schottky (40 V): a low clipper, between germanium and silicon (our fit to Vishay's sheet)

source.licence: Our own fit to the maker's datasheet curve (D-156): the values are Solum Builder's

rating_sources.if_avg: Vishay BAT48 data sheet (formerly General Semiconductor), Document Number 88141, 10-May-02: Forward continuous current 350 mA at 25 °C
rating_sources.vr_max: Vishay BAT48 data sheet (formerly General Semiconductor), Document Number 88141, 10-May-02: Repetitive peak reverse voltage 40 V

fit.sheet: Vishay BAT48 data sheet (formerly General Semiconductor), Document Number 88141, 10-May-02
fit.figure: Ratings and Characteristic Curves: Forward Characteristics, TJ = 25 °C (page 3), read from the PDF's vector drawing
fit.method: IS, N and RS by least squares on V = N·Vt·ln(I/IS) + RS·I (scripts/fit_models.py fit_diode, Vt at 27 °C) over every other curve point, the curve's last point always included; IS held under the sheet's 2 µA leakage limit at 10 V (it fits at 65 nA); CJO is the sheet's 12 pF typical at 1 V; BV 40 V at 100 µA, the sheet's breakdown test
fit.note: The sheet draws the curve as 9 straight segments; their corners are the points. It reads 0.92 V at 500 mA against the sheet's 0.90 V maximum there (a pulse test, above the 350 mA continuous rating and past the drawn curve's 395 mA), so that limit isn't a check
